candidates.title: Prepare triggered emails through a Make scenario

demandEvidence.chore: Set up a Make scenario that sends an email through an SMTP provider when another app triggers it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A sample trigger and test recipient could demonstrate one email, but the post documents no connector setup or implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent workflow consultants may pay for setup help; this request establishes no customer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use a mock trigger and test mailbox; provider configuration and live delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A trigger can start a repeatable send attempt, but a person must verify configuration and approve real recipients; no capability reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The request states the trigger-to-SMTP email task, but gives no frequency, setup detail, corroboration or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the narrow test is conceivable, but the request is brief and no implementation reference supports the connector or delivery steps.

candidates.title: Organize scheduled Pinterest publishing

demandEvidence.chore: Manage editable Pinterest publishing schedules and batches, with CSV import and asset uploads.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Beyond publishing, the node does schedules you can edit in place, batch publishing, CSV import, board access checks, asset uploads, analytics and webhooks for publish results.

ease.reason: A student could test schedule rows and content drafts, but the excerpt describes a built node and supplies no implementation reference for publishing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small marketing service firms may pay for publishing preparation; this project post establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can validate a CSV schedule and draft queue; board access, asset handling and live publishing remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A proposed queue could prepare scheduled items, but people must check assets, board access and publication; no implementation capability reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The excerpt names scheduling, batch publishing, CSV import and uploads, but does not establish repeated external demand or a service buyer.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the project describes scheduling features, but provides little evidence of an unmet recurring chore for the proposed service and no matching implementation reference.

rejected.title: Autonomous Lead Qualification & CRM Enrichment
rejected.reason: The excerpt only labels a completed workflow; it identifies no specific existing manual chore to scope without inventing tasks.

rejected.title: Cloudflare R2 SigV4 signer configuration
rejected.reason: This is a one-off technical configuration question about an S3 signer setting, not a repeated nontechnical service chore; an AI service scope would be invented.

rejected.title: Correct the recipient field in email drafts
rejected.reason: The excerpt reports a single mapping mistake in one draft. It is an isolated bug report, not evidence of a recurring service chore.

steps.message: Assessed all five sealed discussion assignments. Two concrete workflow tasks received full provisional scores but fell below the 6-point threshold; three records lacked a recurring nontechnical chore or described isolated technical issues, so no post is proposed.
